texts.preamble: Biogenetic Drugs Pvt. Ltd vs State Of Gujarat on 21 October, 2021 Author: J.B.Pardiwala Bench: J.B.Pardiwala C/Sca/9214/2020 Order
texts.facts: Alternatively, the writ applicant has also prayed to quash the debarment order dated 4.2.2020 qua other drugs / items of C/SCA/9214/2020 ORDER DATED: 21/10/2021 respective category manufactured by the writ applicant. Short facts giving rise to the present writ application can be, in nutshell, stated as under : 2.1 The respondent No.2 - the Gujarat Medical Services Corporation Ltd. floated a Tender being No.GMSCL/D-596/ RC/2016-17 for supply of Tablet, Capsule, Injection, Miscellaneous and Surgical items. The petitioner participated in the said Tender and offered its bid for various drugs including Polyvitamin Tablet (NFI) Prophylactic being Item Code No.1131 at Serial No.4 of the Tender. The petitioner was found to be lowest bidder for the Item No.1131 at Serial No.4. Thus, the petitioner being a successful bidder, an agreement came to be executed between the petitioner and the respondent No.2 on 16.1.2017. 2.2 Accordingly, the petitioner started supplying the scheduled items being Drug - Polyvitamin Tablets (NFI) Prophylactic. It appears that from the said supply, randomly the Drug Inspector drawn 3 samples from 3 different batches, as under:- Batch No. Manufacturing Date Expiration Date 11127-BGJ15 December, 2017 May, 2019 10127-BGJ15 December, 2017 May, 2019 01018-BGJ15 January, 2018 June 2019 2.3 Those samples thereafter were sent to the Government C/SCA/9214/2020 ORDER DATED: 21/10/2021 Analyst, Food and Drug Laboratory at Vadodara for necessary laboratory test. The Government Laboratory at Vadodara vide its letter dated 9.5.2018 requested the petitioner to provide method of identification and estimation of active ingredient. On 13.6.2018, the petitioner had furnished method of analysis as demanded. The petitioner had also furnished necessary details as demanded by the Government Laboratory at Vadodara. Considering the said details, the Government Laboratory at Vadodara vide its Report dated 4.8.2018 reported that the samples are 'not of standard quality' as defined in the Drugs and Cosmetic Act, 1940 because the samples show no activity of Calcium Pantothenate. It is pertinent to note that so far as Polyvitamin tablets are concerned, activity of Calcium Pantothenate is one of the main components of the drug. The Drug Inspector-cum-Manager of the Gujarat Medical Services Corporation Ltd. vide its letter dated 9.8.2018 intimated the petitioner about the receipt of negative report by the Government Laboratory at Vadodara. 2.4 The petitioner, however, vide letter dated 2.18.2018 countered the report of the Government Laboratory at Vadodara by submitting a report of M/s.Standard Analytical Laboratory (ND) Pvt. Ltd., who had certified that the samples tested of a standard quality. 2.5 The petitioner further vide its reply dated 10.9.2018 raised objection against the Government Laboratory Report and disputed its legality. However, the respondent No.2 herein vide its order C/SCA/9214/2020 ORDER DATED: 21/10/2021 dated 12.3.2019 debarred the petitioner for supply of all tablets for a period of 3 years, which came to be challenged by the writ applicant by way of Writ Application No.7398 of 2019. Biogenetic Drugs Pvt. Ltd vs State Of Gujarat on 21 October, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4866620/ 2 2.6 On 26.4.2019, the learned counsel for the petitioner has stated before this Court that the petitioner has approached the trial court with an application under Section 25(4) of the Drugs and Cosmetic Act for a direction upon the respondents to forward the sample to the Central Drugs Laboratory at Kolkata. 2.7 In view of the aforesaid and upon request being made by the writ applicant on 26.2.2019, the respondent No.2 in its Board meeting resolved to put on hold the debarment of all other tablets till the report of Central Drug Laboratory, Kolkata is declared and that debarment of Polyvitamin tablet only will continue. 2.8 Accordingly, on 29.7.2019, the aforesaid writ application being Special Civil Application No.7398 of 2019 came to be withdrawn by the writ applicant. Ultimately, on 16.9.2019, 17.9.2019 and 23.9.2019, the Central Drug Laboratory at Kolkata submitted its report in negative against the samples sent for C/SCA/9214/2020 ORDER DATED: 21/10/2021 testing, pursuant to the order passed under Section 25(4) of the Drugs and Cosmetic Act by the Sessions Court. Therefore, on 4.2.2020, the Board of Directors of respondent No.2 convened a meeting, wherein at Agenda Item No.30/13, it came to be resolved that upon receipt of the report from the Central Drug Laboratory, Kolkata, the writ applicant - M/s.Biogenetic Drugs Pvt. Ltd. is debarred for 3 years for all the drugs / items of respective category manufactured by them from the date of issuance of debarment order. Thus, being aggrieved and dissatisfied by the aforesaid, the writ applicant has approached this Court by way of present writ application.
texts.arguments: 4) Mr. Thakore, the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the writ applicant has submitted that the Government Analyst as well as Central Drug Laboratory ('CDL'), Kolkata while testing the samples of the writ applicant has not followed "Manufacturers Specification Method of Analysis" and, therefore, the said reports are not legally acceptable. Hence, the action of the respondent No.2 in debarring the writ applicant based on such report, is illegal and deserves to be [LEAKAGE_MASK] and [LEAKAGE_MASK] by this Court. It is further submitted that the reports of the Government Analyst as well as CDL, Kolkata are not in conformity of Rules 45(1) of the Drugs and Cosmetic Rules, 1945 ('the Rules' for short) and C/SCA/9214/2020 ORDER DATED: 21/10/2021 rules framed therein as being beyond reasonable time as prescribed . Therefore, those reports are not good piece of evidence, which could be made sole basis of debarment order passed by the respondent No.2. It has been further submitted that in Poly-vitamins NFI tablets, Calcium Pantothenate is not the only active ingredients. As such there are other nine (09) active ingredients in the said tablets and those ingredients are found to be active, therefore, debarring/black listing the petitioner on the basis of inactive Calcium Pantothenate, is not tenable in the eye of the law. Biogenetic Drugs Pvt. Ltd vs State Of Gujarat on 21 October, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4866620/ 3 4.1 Mr.Thakore further submitted that clause No.3 of debarring policy is misinterpreted by the respondent No.2 and thereby the order of debarring the writ applicant for all his products/items is not tenable in the eye of the law. Thus, in the alternatively Mr. Thakore has submitted that debarment policy/black listing/resolution dated 04.02.2020 could at the most be restricted to item code No.1131 being Polyvitamin Tablet (NFI) Prophylactic rather debarring the writ applicant from its all items/products. 5) Per contra, Ms.Manisha Lavkumar Shah, the learned Government Pleader with Mr.Chintan Dave, the learned Assistant Government Pleader appearing for the respondent No.1 - State has vehemently opposed the writ application by submitting that the debarment order passed by the respondent No.2 is justified being absolutely legal and in consonance with the debarment policy, more particularly, clause No.3 of the debarment policy as C/SCA/9214/2020 ORDER DATED: 21/10/2021 well as government resolution issued by Health and Family Welfare Department on 05.10.2005 being MSP-1099-CM-2-Z. 5.1 Ms.Shah, the learned Government Pleader further submitted that the bare perusal of the Clause-3 of the debarment policy is in no uncertain terms, says that where the drug items supplied by a firm or by a company, is declared as not of a standard quality due to absence of active ingredients, the Firm/Company is debarred for three years for all the drugs/items of the respective category manufactured by them. She has further submitted that in view of the aforesaid, upon the report of the CDL Kolkata under Section 25(4) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, ('the Act') the product of the writ applicant company was found to be not as per the standard quality because of the inactivity of Calcium Pantothenate. Hence, the debarment order passed by the respondent No.2 does not require any interference. She further submitted that two reports i.e. State Analytical Report and CDL, Kolkata, both have confirmed that the samples drawn from the batch product of the writ applicant company are found to be not of a standard quality, therefore, the debarment order based on such report cannot be said to be in any way, illegal and/or illogical. Ms.Shah also submitted that the dispute raised by the present writ applicant with regard to method adopted by the Government Laboratory as well as by CDL Kolkata is not proper, is a highly disputed question of fact, and thereby, a judicial review, under Article 226 of Constitution of India is unwarranted, more so, when as per Section 25(4) of the Act, the report of CDL, Kolkata is a conclusive proof of evidence. C/SCA/9214/2020 ORDER DATED: 21/10/2021 6) We have heard the learned counsel appearing for the respective parties in detailed. The Supreme Court in the case of Dhian Singh v. Municipal Board, Sahranpur, The correct view of the law on the subject is as stated in the decision of the Allahabad High Court in Nagar Mahapalika of Kanpur v. Sri Ram(2) wherein it is observed: C/SCA/9214/2020 ORDER DATED: 21/10/2021 "that the report of the public analyst under s. 13 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 need not contain the mode or particulars of analysis nor the test applied but should contain the result of analysis namely, data from which it can be inferred whether the article of food was or was not adulterated as defined in s. 2(1 ) of the Act." Biogenetic Drugs Pvt. Ltd vs State Of Gujarat on 21 October, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4866620/ 6 13) So far as the contention with regard to the wrong interpretation of the condition no. 3 is concerned, in our considered opinion, the interpretation and the conclusion of condition no. 3 is unambiguous and explicitly clear that drugs/items supplied by firm/company is declared as "not of standard quality" due to absence of active ingredients, for which, the firm/company is debarred for a period of three years for all drugs/items manufactured by them.
